title: The Final Orchid
verdict: Mina Baird was responsible for the disappearance of a sealed packet of judge notes.
intent: Mina Baird wanted to help a favored team anticipate the judges' concerns.
The culprit needed delayed discovery so the object could pass the first search and be recovered later.
action_schema: Use role-specific access: the moot court coordinator requested the reset and kept the cabinet key.
Remove a sealed packet of judge notes from its checked location.
Hide the item in a hollow binder spine in the clerk's cabinet.
Allow incomplete suspicion to fall on distractor suspects.
evidence_cues: a sealed packet of judge notes disappeared from a law school moot court classroom after practice.
The object was confirmed present before the relevant disturbance.
The disappearance occurred within a narrow time window because the hallway camera skipped during a scheduled network reset.
The physical trace was softened glue at the packet corner.
The relevant tool or mechanism was a kettle that had steamed the packet flap.
The item could be concealed in a hollow binder spine in the clerk's cabinet.
The hiding place required insider knowledge because only the moot court coordinator knew the binder spine opened from the bottom.
The access pattern mattered because the moot court coordinator requested the reset and kept the cabinet key.
The motive was to help a favored team anticipate the judges' concerns.
distractor_cues: a student arguing about the practice score
A visible conflict is suspicious but insufficient without timing and mechanism.
A bulky object or nervous behavior is insufficient unless it explains the hidden container.
